messages:
ashley: Hey team, customer reports SDK estimate = 120 tokens but invoice shows 164 tokens for same request. They included curl + payload. Can someone double-check quickly? :confused:

mike: Can you paste the exact curl and which SDK estimator they used (node/python)? Also invoice id?

ashley: Invoice ID INV-2026-0342, customer using node SDK 0.9.3 estimator. Curl they sent:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-xxxx' 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
 -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the report in 3 bullets."}],"max_tokens":150}'
```
They say local estimator prints 120 tokens. Invoice shows 164.

billing-bot: Automated note: invoice INV-2026-0342 has a usage line on 2026-03-11 13:02 UTC, 164 total tokens, customer account acct-8731.

jordan: First guess: system message + any hidden tool call / function response tokens? Did they use function calling or a toolchain that returns hidden assistant messages?

ashley: Customer says no explicit functions. They did mention using streaming in app but this request was non-streaming.

mike: Two quick repro checks: 1) SDK estimator usually excludes server-injected preambles (e.g., platform assistant messages) unless you opt-in. 2) Metering counts everything the server saw, including any injected system/context and tool outputs. Ask them to include full request body the server received (we have server logs if they give timestamp).

ashley: Pasted server request body from logs (sanitized keys):
```json
{"model":"rwd-3b","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."},{"role":"assistant","content":"<hidden:policy>"},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the report in 3 bullets."}],"max_tokens":150}
```
They didn't expect the extra assistant message.

eng-matt: That extra assistant preamble is likely our runtime injecting a safety/context prompt for that tenant (we rolled a per-tenant policy preamble in Feb). SDK estimator won't see that unless you call the metering helper after the final merged payload. This accounts for roughly ~40 tokens depending on wording.

mike: Also check for tool output: if the runtime executed an internal tranform or reranker that appended text to the messages before generation, those tokens would be billed. Confirmed?

ashley: Customer confirms they have a server-side policy preamble enabled via console (they thought it was "metadata-only"). They didn't realize it was being prepended as an assistant message.

jordan: Quick repro I ran: local node estimator reported 118 for the two-message input. When I submitted the same payload to our API (with tenant preamble) invoice-style metering=159. So matches. Repro steps: include tenant preamble in messages array and run estimator -> counts align with invoice.

ashley: Customer is surprised because console flag name was ambiguous. They're requesting doc clarity and a way for SDK to surface injected tokens so estimator matches billing.

eng-matt: Action items: 1) Support to explain cause to customer and provide itemized token breakdown for that invoice line (we can show 'user prompt', 'system preamble', 'model completion' segments). 2) Product: rename console flag and add UI tooltip clarifying injection. 3) SDK: add optional call to fetch merged payload for metering (or provide a flag to include injected system messages in local estimator).

support-ops: I'll take the customer-facing message and attach a token breakdown. Proposed reply: "Thanks — we found a server-side 'assistant' preamble injected for your tenant which added ~44 tokens. Our meter counts the final merged payload while the SDK estimator only saw your original messages. We're escalating to product/SDK to improve visibility."

ashley: Customer updated with breakdown and accepted explanation. They asked how to avoid surprises for future runs.

eng-matt: Short-term mitigation: turn off tenant preamble or use preview endpoint that returns merged prompt (we should document). Long-term SDK change tracked in RFC #1542 to surface merged payload for metering.

mike: Logging note: add a subtle log line in the request path when we inject any assistant/system preamble so support + customers can see it in request logs by default.

support-ops: Marking resolved for billing. Will open product ticket for flag rename and SDK ticket for opt-in merged-payload estimator. :white_check_mark:
